summary.en: Use sets for unique values, membership and group comparisons, and frozenset for immutable groups.
summary.bn: অনন্য মান, সদস্যপদ আর দলের তুলনায় সেট ব্যবহার করো; অপরিবর্তনীয় দলের জন্য frozenset নাও।

notes: Set and frozenset operations in this lesson work on Python 3.10–3.12. Set iteration order is not guaranteed across runs or versions, so numeric reports explicitly sort their results.

sections.title: Ask who belongs, rather than which position
Equality decides whether a member already exists
Compare groups with explicit output order
Change a register or freeze a group
Preserve the information your problem needs
Membership is stable; display order is not promised

examples.title: Keep one copy of each roll
examples.explanationHtml: Repeated rolls collapse into three distinct members. sorted creates an ordered list for display because set iteration has no guaranteed position order. Membership reports True for 18 and False for 99.

examples.title: Compare two workshop groups
examples.explanationHtml: Union includes everyone; intersection includes 2 and 4. Difference keeps 1 from robotics alone. Symmetric difference keeps 1 and 3, who joined exactly one workshop. The final subset test is True.

examples.title: Update a membership register
examples.explanationHtml: Adding 12 twice still stores it once. update visits all values in its input. discard tolerates missing 99, whereas remove requires its argument to exist. The remaining rolls are 12 and 25.

examples.title: Store immutable teams
examples.explanationHtml: A frozenset cannot be edited and can itself be a set member. Order does not affect equality, so the two equal two-person teams count once. Union produces a new group containing 12, 18 and 25.

practice.title: Distinct roll count
practice.statementHtml: Read a line of integer rolls, possibly empty. Print the number of distinct rolls.
hints: Convert the parsed integers to a set before measuring length.

practice.title: Shared participants
practice.statementHtml: Read two lines of integer participant IDs. Print the IDs present in both groups in ascending order on one line, or a blank line for no overlap.
hints: Intersect the sets, then sort only for display.

practice.title: Missing submissions
practice.statementHtml: Read registered integer rolls on the first line and submitted rolls on the second. Print registered rolls with no submission in ascending order, each once. Unknown submitted rolls do not affect the answer.
hints: Set difference is directional: subtract submitted from registered.

practice.title: Count distinct teams
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20, then n lines of integer team-member IDs. A line may be empty. Teams with the same members are equal regardless of order or repetition. Print the number of distinct teams.
hints: A frozenset can represent a team inside the outer set.

quiz.prompt: How many members remain after repeated insertion?
quiz.explanation: A set keeps at most one member for each equal hashable value.

quiz.prompt: Which IDs belong only to the left group?
quiz.explanation: Difference retains members of the left set that are absent from the right set.
Order and duplicate input do not affect set equality; the outer set keeps one equal team.
quiz.code:
a = frozenset([1, 2])
b = frozenset([2, 1, 1])
print(a == b)
print(len({a, b}))

quiz.prompt: Which expression creates an empty set?
quiz.explanation: Empty braces create a dictionary; set() explicitly creates an empty set.

quiz.prompt: Which operation keeps members found in exactly one of two sets?
quiz.explanation: Symmetric difference excludes shared members and includes members unique to either side.

quiz.prompt: Which missing-member operation is safe without a prior membership test?
quiz.explanation: discard ignores an absent member; remove raises KeyError.

quiz.prompt: Why sort a numeric set before printing its members?
options: Set order is not a display-order guarantee
A set always stores descending values
quiz.explanation: The set has no sequence positions; sorted provides a deliberate numeric ordering.

quiz.prompt: Which object can be a set member?
quiz.explanation: frozenset is hashable; the mutable containers in the other choices are not.

quiz.prompt: What does left <= right test for sets?
options: Every left member also belongs to right
left has fewer members regardless of contents
The first left value is smaller
Both sets have the same insertion order
quiz.explanation: Subset comparison tests membership inclusion, not sequence order or size alone.

quiz.prompt: When is a set a poor replacement for a marks list?
options: When repeated marks and student order must be preserved
When checking whether a roll is registered
quiz.explanation: A set discards duplicates and offers no student-position correspondence.

quiz.prompt: What is the usual average cost of set membership lookup?
options: Constant time, with possible worse collision cases
quiz.explanation: Hash lookup is usually constant time, but worst cases can be linear.

keyPoints.en: Sets keep unique hashable members without sequence indexes.
keyPoints.bn: সেটে অনন্য হ্যাশযোগ্য সদস্য থাকে; সিকোয়েন্সের মতো ইনডেক্স থাকে না।

keyPoints.en: Union combines groups and intersection finds shared members.
keyPoints.bn: ইউনিয়ন দল মেলায়, আর ইন্টারসেকশন সবার সাধারণ সদস্য খুঁজে দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Difference depends on which set is on the left.
keyPoints.bn: ডিফারেন্সে বাম পাশে কোন সেট আছে তা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।

keyPoints.en: discard tolerates absence, while remove raises KeyError.
keyPoints.bn: সদস্য না থাকলে discard কিছু করে না, কিন্তু remove-এ KeyError হয়।

keyPoints.en: frozenset is an immutable, hashable set value.

examQuestions.question: Compare set and frozenset, including their suitability as dictionary keys.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Both describe unique members without sequence positions. set allows edits and is unhashable. frozenset disallows edits and is hashable, so it can be a dictionary key or another set member.

examQuestions.question: For A={1,2,3} and B={3,4}, give A-B, A&B and A^B in ascending order.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A-B gives [1, 2], the intersection gives [3], and symmetric difference gives [1, 2, 4]. Shared member 3 is excluded from symmetric difference.

examQuestions.question: Find missing rolls when registered is [2,2,5,8] and submitted is [5,9].
examQuestions.answerHtml:
registered = {2, 2, 5, 8}
submitted = {5, 9}
print(*sorted(registered - submitted))

The report is 2 8. Duplicate registration 2 counts once, and unknown submitted roll 9 does not become missing work.
